slides.title: The Pipeline Needed More Than One Person.
slides.subtitle: An outreach workflow for a small team, told as a retrospective
slides.caption: At an executive ground-transportation company, one person was the sales pipeline: finding companies, writing the first message, sending it, following up. The ask was a daily queue a small team could share.

slides.title: Three questions a shared queue raises.
slides.subtitle: Who sees which leads? Whose name goes on a message? What may a model change?
slides.caption: On 14 June 2026 the client described who would work the pipeline: one person seeing everything, a second owning Texas, Iowa handed to a new hire. That made it a multi-person problem.

The daily queue for one representative, scoped to one state, on a keyless local copy at the pinned commit with invented rows. The territory rule runs on the server: the user's states win over anything the query asks for.

slides.title: Territory beyond the screen.
slides.subtitle: List, chips, export, detail and queue, clamped on the server.
slides.caption: Verified over the API with a minted token per user, 25 of 25 checks on 24 June 2026. Not through a browser login: every browser was signed in as one shared administrator account.

One email step: a template draft a person reviews before anything is sent. At the last commit the draft speaks in the campaign's sender voice, and mail leaves through four guards as that campaign's mailbox.

rows: leads in the pipeline on 18 September 2026, by the platform's own daily report; 0 emails sent in each September report read, each covering the previous day
live campaign emails to 29 June 2026, every one logged to a campaign and a lead
meetings, proposals and won recorded on 20 June 2026 and in the September reports read
slides.caption: Counts with dates, from the repository's own log and the platform's own report. No revenue, conversion or hours figure exists, and none is claimed.
Report an issue: a model may apply one of five bounded actions, or hold. Here, with no model key, the issue is logged and held for a person, which is the honest keyless outcome.

slides.title: What remains unresolved.
slides.subtitle: The shared login, six unscoped routes, a dormant unguarded mail path.
slides.caption: Sign-out, per-user signatures and drafts as the signed-in representative were built locally after the last commit and never committed or deployed. The project was sunset in September 2026.
